# filename: parse_pdf_seahorse.py
import pdfplumber
import re

pdf_path = "/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/67e8878b-5cef-4375-804e-e6291fdbe78a.pdf"

rows = []
current_type = None
rating_pattern = re.compile(r"([0-5])(?:\s|$)")

with pdfplumber.open(pdf_path) as pdf:
    for page in pdf.pages:
        text = page.extract_text() or ""
        for line in text.splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if line in ["Hotels", "Motels", "Villas", "Guesthouses", "Inns", "Resorts", "Cottages", "B&Bs"]:
                current_type = line
                continue
            # Attempt to capture name and rating on lines
            m = rating_pattern.search(line)
            if current_type and m:
                rating = float(m.group(1))
                # Name is the part before the rating
                name = line[:m.start()].strip()
                if name:
                    rows.append({"Type": current_type, "Name": name, "Rating": rating})

# Show sample output and counts
print("Sample extracted rows (first 12):")
for r in rows[:12]:
    print(f"{r['Type']}, {r['Name']}, {r['Rating']}")

from collections import Counter
cnt = Counter([r['Type'] for r in rows])
print("\nTotal counts:")
for k, v in cnt.items():
    print(f"{k}: {v}")
